items.note: One-group pre-post quasi-experiment: 28 EFL student teachers used ChatGPT, Jenni and Whimsical, and descriptive and narrative writing was scored for fluency, accuracy and originality; no control group, so likely fails eligibility at full text.

Two field experiments on LLM-assisted cover letters measure signal quality and interview invitations; cover letters are a borderline creative task and a standardization outcome may exist, so the full text must confirm who is assigned and whether any diversity or quality score fits scope (abstract from Crossref).

Field study with 75 children aged 9-10 assigned to hand-made closed cues, GPT-3 closed cues, or GPT-3 open cues for curious (divergent) question-asking training; questions were annotated by humans; AI generates training content rather than assisting the task directly, and the outcome is creativity-adjacent.

User study of LLM-assisted essay writing (heavy LLM use raised neutral-stance essays by about 70 percent; heavy users self-report less creativity) plus LLM revisions of 2021 essays and AI peer reviews; search notes say 100 Prolific participants randomized to no-LLM (45) or gpt-4o-mini (55) with embedding homogenization, not in the abstract.

Three intact tenth-grade classes (25 each) randomly allocated to classroom training, AI-tools training, or control, with the Torrance Test given pre, post and at follow-up; randomization is at the class level with only three classes, and the TTCT is likely taken without AI (after_ai); abstract in Arabic.

Mixed-methods study with 80 EFL undergraduates in GenAI and control groups; creative writing scored for originality, cognitive flexibility and expressive innovation (abstract from the journal page; DOI does not resolve in Crossref or OpenAlex).

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar elided, Europe PMC no hit); title suggests a study of generative AI and creativity in EFL teaching, design unknown, classified as experiment only to send it to full-text review.

2x2 RCT with 1,053 Bocconi first-years crossing ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access with causal-reasoning training on a merchandising business problem; experts rated solutions and diversity of ideas was measured (abstract from RePEc CEPR DP 21882; also an OpenAI report PDF).

Lab experiment randomly assigning participants to ChatGPT access or not on an open-ended writing task, crossed with incentive schemes; Prolific raters scored creativity; abstract gives no N (search notes say 360); same work as Ca' Foscari DSE WP 16/2026.

Eighteen students wrote essays with (9) or without (9) ChatGPT-3.5; outcomes are grades, authenticity and between-essay similarity; far below 50 participants; arXiv 2302.04536 and EdArXiv are earlier versions.
